svg.title: P008 · Price band labels
svg.desc: One row per product with one budget label. The Pen costs 199 and enters Budget. The other four rows still need a label. The Book at 200 and Bag at 699.50 both enter Mid. The Watch at 700 misses this band. The Watch becomes Premium. Mystery has a NULL price and receives Unknown. All five products stay. FROM Products · one table is enough. Each product gets one band from its own sale price. The catalogue already contains its ID, name and price, including products with a missing price.
svg.text: One row per product with one budget label.
Which band owns exactly 200? What about exactly 700?
A triangle marks an example to follow. A dark source band spans its columns. ƒ marks a calculated value. Deeper cell colors mark the values to
follow. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.

svg.text: The Pen costs 199 and enters Budget. The other four rows still need a label.
The Book at 200 and Bag at 699.50 both enter Mid. The Watch at 700 misses this band.
How do the remaining rows get labels?
The Watch becomes Premium. Mystery has a NULL price and receives Unknown. All five products stay.
